answer: Physical AI refers to AI systems that perceive, understand, reason about, and act in the real world through motor skills, rather than operating only on digital text or images — think robots, humanoids, drones, and self-driving vehicles. It requires models that grasp physical properties like gravity, friction, inertia, and cause-and-effect, increasingly built with world foundation models and vision-language-action (VLA) models. A typical development pipeline uses 3D simulation and digital twins to generate synthetic training data before the trained policy is deployed to real machines.
